name: Ruthless Negotiation
description:
Exile a card from target opponent's hand. Draw a card.

Flashback {4}{B} (cast from your graveyard for this cost; the card is exiled instead of going to your graveyard when it resolves this way). No further printed effect could be determined for this casting mode from the nodes given.
assumptions: Read node E (owner:opp, thing:any, flags:target, hand->exile) as "exile a card from target opponent's hand," attaching the targeting to the opponent being targeted rather than the card itself, since the schema doesn't distinguish who does the choosing.
Read node B (self, stack->gy, under root A) as the ordinary unprinted resting state of a resolved sorcery, not a printed effect.

Read the {4}{B} altCost[gy] plus node D (self, stack->exile, under root C) as a Flashback-style keyword, since exile-after-resolving-from-graveyard is Flashback's defining behavior, even though no keyword name is given in the nodes.
couldNotDerive: Whether casting via the alternate cost from the graveyard (root C) also exiles a card from the opponent's hand and/or causes a draw — root C's only step is D (self to exile); nodes E and F are reachable only from root A (the hand cast), so per the flow graph the hand-cast mode produces the exile+draw effect and the graveyard-cast mode produces no printed effect at all beyond removing itself from the game.
Who chooses which card is exiled from the opponent's hand (caster, opponent, or random) — the 'target' flag only establishes that a choice/targeting occurs, not who makes it.
notes:
Decomposition gap, not a schema gap or agent error. Real card (forge-model/data/ruthless-negotiation.txt): a single spell ability `A:SP$ ChangeZone | Origin$ Hand | Destination$ Exile | ValidTgts$ Opponent | Chooser$ Targeted | ChangeNum$ 1 | Mandatory$ True | SubAbility$ DBDraw` with `SVar:DBDraw:DB$ Draw | ConditionDefined$ Self | ConditionPresent$ Card.wasCastFromGraveyard | ConditionCompare$ EQ1`, plus `K:Flashback:4 B`. Oracle text: "Target opponent exiles a card from their hand. If this spell was cast from a graveyard, draw a card. Flashback {4}{B}". Two concrete bugs in this card's edges.json (and by extension whatever forgeTranslate.ts logic produced them):

1. Node E (the ChangeZone/exile-from-hand effect, matching the `A:SP$ ChangeZone` line's core effect) is the SAME spell ability regardless of which cost paid it — Forge does not define a second, separate ability for the Flashback cast. The packet's flow only lists E as a step under root A (hand cast); it is never a step under root C (graveyard/flashback cast). E needs to be reachable from both roots.

2. F (the `emit draw` node, corresponding to `SVar:DBDraw`) is gated in Forge by `ConditionPresent$ Card.wasCastFromGraveyard | ConditionCompare$ EQ1` — the draw fires ONLY when the spell was cast via Flashback/from the graveyard, never on a normal hand cast. The packet instead chains F as a step of E, which itself only descends from root A (the hand-cast root). As decomposed, this inverts the real condition: the draw would trigger on the hand cast and never on the flashback cast — exactly backwards from `Card.wasCastFromGraveyard`. F's edge needs to carry a condition tying it to the graveyard-cast path (e.g. reachable from/conditioned on C or D, with a `cond:cast-from-graveyard` flag) instead of unconditionally following E under A.

Everything else lines up: mana cost {B}, type Sorcery, and the Flashback {4}{B} alt cost (`K:Flashback:4 B`) with its built-in exile-after-resolution (node D under root C) are all faithfully captured. The blind reconstruction above correctly flagged the C-branch's missing effect and the ambiguity as "could not derive" rather than inventing the condition, which is exactly the gap: the packet as given genuinely underdetermines (and actively misdirects, via E/F's placement) the real wasCastFromGraveyard-gated draw.
